key_insight: Cova-PINN improves fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer predictions by enforcing conservation across thermal interaction paths, not just within separately sampled fluid and solid domains.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINN-based surrogate modeling more reliable for heat exchanger design, especially when accurate outlet temperature and energy balance matter more than visually plausible temperature fields.
method: Uses a multi-domain PINN for fluid and solid regions in complex geometries.
Adds cross-domain composite control-volume conservation constraints at local scales.
Imposes paired-wall closure at the exchanger scale to preserve end-to-end heat transfer.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on four TPMS heat exchangers and a DualMS geometry, Cova-PINN outperformed multiple CHT, optimization-oriented, and complex-geometry PINN baselines, cutting average outlet-temperature error by 37.7% and device-level closure error by 60.2% versus the closest baseline.
watch_item: The added conservation constraints may increase implementation complexity and require careful balancing of local and global loss terms to avoid training instability.
paper_title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
